mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the Consumer Price Index (CPI) over the past two months signals inflationary pressure, leading to tighter monetary policy expectations and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or CPIAUCSL increases do not correlate with tightening monetary policy.

mechanism_narrative: A significant increase in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) over the past month signals weakening labor market conditions, which leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or UNRATE increases do not correlate with economic downturns.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in housing starts (HOUST) over the past two months signals strengthening demand in the housing market, which is a leading indicator of broader economic growth and positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in > 40% of periods with sustained HOUST increases, or HOUST increases do not correlate with broader economic growth.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in industrial production (INDPRO) over the past month signals weakening supply-side conditions, which leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 5-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or INDPRO declines do not correlate with supply-side contractions.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) above 2% signals a tightening monetary policy, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or FEDFUNDS increases above 2% do not correlate with tightening monetary policy.

mechanism_narrative: A joint increase in real personal consumption expenditures (RSAFS) and nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) over the past month signals strengthening demand and labor market conditions, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS and PAYEMS both increase > 0.5% MoM
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in > 40% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or joint increases in RSAFS and PAYEMS do not correlate with economic expansion.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) combined with an increase in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) over the past month signals weakening labor market conditions, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS decreases > 0.5% MoM and UNRATE increases > 0.3pp
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or the combination of PAYEMS decrease and UNRATE increase does not correlate with economic downturns.

mechanism_narrative: A significant increase in real GDP (GDPC1) over the past quarter signals strong economic growth, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days, but only during a regime of economic expansion.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 60-day returns in > 40% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or GDPC1 increases do not correlate with economic expansion.
